title: 1. Timely Injury Reporting
text: Work-related injuries and incidents are reported internally to the appropriate person immediately or as soon as practicable after they occur, regardless of their apparent severity.
validation: Average time from injury to supervisor notification and carrier/TPA reporting; % reported within target timeframe.
improve: Establish a clear expectation that all injuries and incidents are reported internally the same day they occur, regardless of severity, and confirm that supervisors and employees know exactly who to notify.

title: 2. Supervisor Response and Incident Investigation
text: When an injury or incident occurs, supervisors respond promptly, document what happened, and investigate the contributing factors — not simply who was at fault.
validation: % of incidents investigated within target timeframe; completeness of root-cause and corrective-action documentation.
improve: Build a simple, repeatable incident-investigation process so supervisors document what happened and identify contributing factors, not just who was at fault.

title: 3. Medical Direction and Provider Coordination
text: Employees and supervisors know where an injured employee should receive appropriate medical care, and the organization coordinates the initial treatment process.
validation: % of cases using designated/appropriate providers where permitted; time from injury to coordinated medical follow-up.
improve: Make sure employees and supervisors know, in advance, where injured employees should go for initial treatment, and coordinate that first medical visit directly rather than leaving it to the employee.

title: 4. Return-to-Work Management
text: The organization actively identifies meaningful transitional or modified-duty work to help injured employees return safely and productively as soon as medically appropriate.
validation: Days from injury to modified-duty offer; % of eligible injured employees returned to transitional duty; duration of modified duty.
improve: Create a standing list of modified or transitional-duty tasks so a return-to-work offer is ready before it's needed, rather than improvised after each injury.

title: 5. Claims Oversight and Reserve Management
text: Open workers' compensation claims are reviewed regularly with the broker, carrier, claims administrator, or other appropriate parties to monitor progress, barriers, and financial exposure.
validation: Open-claim review cadence; age of open claims; time since last carrier/TPA update; significant reserve changes; documented reserve discussions and escalation actions.
improve: Put a recurring claims-review meeting on the calendar with your broker, carrier, or claims administrator so open claims, reserve changes, and stalled cases get regular visibility.

title: 6. Safety Leadership and Employee Engagement
text: Leaders and supervisors consistently reinforce safe work practices, involve employees in identifying risks, and hold themselves and others accountable for safety performance.
validation: Frequency of safety leadership touchpoints; employee participation; closure rate for identified safety actions.
improve: Give supervisors a simple, recurring way to reinforce safety expectations and involve employees directly in identifying hazards, rather than relying on posters or annual training alone.

title: 7. Near-Miss Reporting and Continuous Improvement
text: Employees are encouraged to report near misses and unsafe conditions, and the organization reviews those reports to prevent future injuries.
validation: Near-misses reported per period; % investigated; corrective-action closure rate and recurrence tracking.
improve: Create an easy, low-friction way for employees to report near misses and unsafe conditions, and make sure those reports are actually reviewed and acted on.

title: 8. Payroll Reporting and Classification Accuracy
text: Payroll, employee duties, classifications, overtime, and other remuneration information are reviewed for accuracy before being reported to the workers' compensation carrier or payroll provider.
validation: Audit exceptions; classification corrections; payroll variance; reconciliation accuracy and timeliness.
improve: Add a regular check of payroll, job classifications, and overtime reporting before it goes to the carrier or payroll provider, to catch errors before they affect premium.

title: 9. Broker Strategy and Underwriter Engagement
text: The organization works with its insurance advisor throughout the policy year — not only at renewal — to review losses, operational changes, risk-improvement efforts, and the organization's underwriting story.
validation: Documented stewardship and claim-review meetings; pre-renewal planning cadence; broker involvement in carrier/TPA escalations; completion of underwriting action items.
improve: Move the relationship with your insurance advisor from a once-a-year renewal conversation to a year-round one that includes loss reviews, risk-improvement planning, and underwriting strategy.

title: 10. Leadership Accountability and Performance Review
text: Leadership regularly reviews workers' compensation performance and assigns clear responsibility for improving the operational behaviors that influence injuries, claims, and insurance costs.
validation: Quarterly review of CCB metrics; documented owners, due dates, and completion of corrective actions.
improve: Assign clear ownership for workers' compensation performance and put a recurring leadership review on the calendar so these behaviors are actively managed, not just assumed.
